image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a grey whale's back and dorsal area surfacing in green water. The skin is dark grey with characteristic white mottling and barnacle patches. A distinct longitudinal ridge runs along the spine. No dorsal fin is visible, consistent with the species. A small portion of a yellow object (likely a kayak or boat) is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up of the mid-back/dorsal region; the head and blowholes are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey coloration with irregular white patches indicative of barnacles/callosities.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no triangular dorsal fin. Instead, a series of low humps (knuckles) and a longitudinal ridge are visible along the spine, matching the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The curvature of the back suggests a massive, robust cylindrical body shape typical of large cetaceans.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed visually across the entire visible surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth and interior of the whale are not visible; baleen cannot be seen.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral lower body and are not visible in this dorsal view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface texture appears uneven and rough, consistent with the presence of callosities and barnacles rather than smooth skin.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The dark line running along the spine appears slightly too uniform and 'painted on' compared to the organic irregularity of the surrounding skin texture. It lacks subtle depth variation.
The yellow object (likely a kayak) has an undefined, melting edge where it meets the water and the whale. It lacks clear structural definition or realistic reflection/refraction.
The water ripples in the upper right show slight inconsistency in perspective and focus, appearing somewhat smudged rather than optically sharp.
